label: directed communication to
definition: X directs information, speech, a request, warning or advice to addressee Y.
scope_notes: Tell, urge, ask, notify, persuade, address, testify-before and speaking-to qualify. Meeting, cooperation, statements about Y and physical transfers alone do not. Send/submit/give with no object are ambiguous unless other rows establish communication.

facts.reason: Mr. Greenspan tells, addresses and testifies before the Senate Banking Committee, with testimony-to support in the required direction.
Bush directly tells, asks and urges Congress. The administration attribution and unspecified send/submit rows are additional evidence, not needed to infer the direct communication.
Republicans explicitly urge Mr. Clinton, establishing directed communication; accusations and action against him are separate meanings.
Torre explicitly asks Rivera and summons him. Use, commentary about Rivera and go-to descriptions add other meanings.

The direct send-to row omits the object. Meeting and referral-by do not establish an outgoing message, and the convoluted testimony/call path does not clearly make Lewinsky the communicator to Jordan.
facts.reviewer_question: What did Ms. Lewinsky send to Vernon Jordan, and does the underlying text establish communication from her to him?
